look_here_first: Grayish thorny shrub with relatively straight stems, scattered less-curved prickles, 1–2 pairs of pinnae, and fragrant pink globose flower heads.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Fabaceae/Mimosa: bipinnate leaves, pulvini that can drive touch-sensitive movement in several species, globose heads of many tiny flowers, and segmented/prickly legumes. Habit, prickle placement, pinna count, and pod structure are especially useful.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: prickles scattered rather than paired at nodes

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: pods often longer and stipitate at base

lookalikes.differences: Best compared with M. texana: borealis is grayer with straighter stems, less-hooked prickles, and usually longer more stipitate pods.
